riskTone.label: NEUTRAL
riskTone.rationale: FTSE 100 flat with mixed sector moves; US-Iran tension adds mild risk-off pressure, offset by awaited inflation data providing no clear directional bias.

briefing.briefing: Starting with the currency picture: GBPUSD is up +0.44% today, sitting at the 89th percentile of its last 20 days — meaning sterling is unusually strong right now. Because UK100 and GBP move in opposite directions (a stronger pound makes overseas earnings worth less when converted back), this is a headwind [drag] for the FTSE; the snapshot flags this as a BEARISH GBP impact on the index, though the overall FX read is softened to NEUTRAL at the index level. The dominant bullish forces are coming from commodities: copper is surging +2.44%, which is directly lifting miners like Rio Tinto, Glencore, and Anglo American — all top-index heavyweights — while Brent crude is up +0.94%, supporting Shell and BP. European markets (DAX +0.62%, EuroStoxx +0.77%) and US futures (S&P 500 +0.52%) are all pointing the same way, which is an encouraging [agreeing] backdrop. Gilts [UK government bonds] are slightly calmer, with the 10-year yield down 2 basis points [a tiny unit of interest rate movement]; long-end stress is absent, so no fiscal alarm bells. The only notable recent headline (22.9 hours ago) cited a US-Iran flare-up keeping energy stocks in the spotlight but leaving the index broadly flat — nothing fresh in the last few hours that changes the picture. The key wrinkle today is US CPI [inflation data for America] at 13:30 BST — this is a HIGH-impact event that has already suppressed the model's conviction, because if inflation comes in hotter than expected it could rattle global markets quickly. The ORB [Opening Range Breakout — a trade taken when price moves decisively above or below the first-candle range] already broke DOWN through its low (orbBrokenDirection: DOWN), meaning the 08:00 setup played to the short side this morning. However, price is currently at 10,515 — above both the ORB high of 10,488 and the overnight high of 10,499.9 — suggesting the market has since reversed and pushed higher. Crucially, the 14-day average daily range [how far the index typically moves in a day] of 128.1 points is already 104% used, meaning today's range is essentially exhausted; chasing new moves is dangerous. Confidence is 4/10 — the bullish commodity tailwinds are real, but the CPI print at 13:30 BST could flip everything, the GBP is at a 20-day high working against the index, and the day's range is already fully spent. A softer-than-expected CPI would boost the bullish case; a hot print would likely reverse gains sharply. For the ORB trade specifically, the setup already played out this morning (breakdown, then reversal), the range is exhausted, and with a market-moving CPI report just hours away this is firmly a stand-aside afternoon — protect any morning profits and wait for tomorrow's cleaner slate. On Wednesday at 07:00 BST, UK GDP data drops — another HIGH-impact event — so position sizing [how much you risk per trade] should remain conservative into mid-week. Key levels to watch: ORB high 10,488 and overnight high 10,499.9 as near support now that price has broken above them; prior day high 10,526.3 as the next resistance [ceiling]; and ORB low 10,447.4 / overnight low 10,414.8 as downside anchors if CPI spooks the market. The one thing to remember today: the range is already 104% used and CPI prints at 13:30 — this is a news-event afternoon, not a trend-trading afternoon.
